svg.text: IN: THE COPPER, ALL 97 LETTERS, THE 24 KNOWN PLACES IN ACCENT
K4's two marks: in rows of 7, five of its six doubled letters start in one column; in rows of 21, 11 letter pairs repeat straight down
rows of 21: cells in a repeating vertical pair (11 repeats)
Each mark alone is rare. A recipe that explains K4 should make both at once.
Each recipe below enciphered 20,000 stretches of Carter's English; counts are how many showed each mark.
width-7 columnar, then ciphertext autokey lag 1 + period-7 key
width-7 quarter turn, then period-14 key
K3-rule move, then column-plus-row key, width 7
period-14 key, then width-7 quarter turn
width-7 quarter turn, then period-21 key
width-7 columnar, then ciphertext autokey lag 21 + period-7 key
period-21 key, then width-7 quarter turn

the column-plus-row key in rows of 7 makes the doublet column 52 times in 20,000, about the rate of random letters (32) and shuffled K4 (38): so it does not explain the column, as 0087 assumed it would
OUT: NO READING; NO RECIPE MAKES BOTH MARKS
